payload.text: ¡Ay, amigo! Forty-five, forty-four, forty-five... we are going in circles, and the van is honking. No hard feelings, ¿eh? We close the suitcase today. Paco sends a hug, Nando sends two. Maybe another plaza, another day, another price. ¡Hasta luego, amigo! Keep your pesetas warm.
Eighty-five remains a fantasy, señor, however gracefully offered. Sixty-five pesetas — and I do not say such numbers twice lightly. The album is open, the page empty. Shall we finish like gentlefolk?

"¡Amigo! Perfect timing—" "—we were just about to close the case!" Paco flips it open, Nando leans in. "San Francisco el Grande, look at that gold leaf, it breathes! A collector in Toledo cried when we took it from him."

"One hundred eighty-seven pesos. Today only, while our hands are still shaking."
Eighty, señor? No. Sixty-seven pesetas — and that is me being generous, not forgetful of the figures. The page in my album stays empty only a little longer. Decide, por favor, elegantly.
Buenas, señor — we have been dancing a while. Sixty-nine pesetas, and I say it without pleasure in repeating myself. The page in Salamanca waits. Shall we end this elegantly, por favor?

"¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come — look what we have here! La Sala Pentagrama, pristine, beautiful, makes grown collectors weep. For you, 187 P. Paco, show him—" "—I'm showing, I'm showing!" Listen, the police— ah, the *taxi*, the taxi is waiting outside, engine running. Decide now, eh?

Te acuerdas bien. Yo también. La Galería son treinta y tres. Veinte es para soñar, chaval.
Setenta y una pesetas por el Museo Lázaro Galdiano, señor. Es mi última palabra — si la rechaza, cierro el álbum y me retiro sin rencor. Decida ahora, por favor, con elegancia.
Buenas tardes. How very nice. You carry El Ángel Caído — El Retiro, my beloved park. I know that print run exactly, and I know what it deserves. Sixty-one pesetas, señor, and it joins my album today.

"¡La Reina! Ay, Nando, he's dreaming of other cards already—" "—but the Pentagrama is here, in his hands, mira!" Listen, amigo, 167 P and the taxi driver stops shouting at us. Beautiful piece, you'll thank us at the next tournament. ¿Sí? Quick, quick, before Paco changes his mind!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, the handsome one. Come, come, look at this beauty: San Francisco el Grande, holy and rare, barely out of the suitcase. For you, because your face I like — 187 P. Say sí quickly, the crowd is coming, verdad, hermano?
Buenas tardes. El Retiro, sí, siempre me conmueve. El Palacio de Velázquez es una pieza bonita, lo admito, aunque conozco bien su tirada. Le ofrezco 22 P por ella, y con mucho gusto.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look, this one is my Té Moruno — a pretty card, yes? For you, five P, and you start your album today. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

¡Amigo, amiga! Paco here, and this is Nando — don't blink, we move fast. Look at this beauty: Puesto del Rastro, yours for 4 P. The team next door was sniffing around it, hands already in their pockets... but we like your face better. Say the word, and it's wrapped.

"¡La Reina, la Reina! Nando, he sings the same song—" "—and we don't have her, corazón!" What we have is la Sala Pentagrama, warm in your hands. 155 P, amigo, and the driver outside stops honking at us. Say sí, quick — Paco's already halfway to the door!
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Querido amigo, mis números no bailan. La pieza es bonita, sí, pero su tirada no es modesta. Veintidós P, como le dije, y la coloco junto a mis bailarinas del Retiro con mucho gusto.

"¡Otra vez la Reina! Nando, he's in love with a card we don't carry—" "—and meanwhile la Sala Pentagrama is getting cold, hombre!" 145 P, amigo. The driver's already pulling away, we're running with the suitcase. Say sí now, or we tell this story in another city!
Qué imagen tan bonita me pinta usted, amigo. Pero el domingo no cambia la tirada. Suba yo un escalón, por cortesía: veintitrés P. Y el Palacio queda en su página del Retiro, donde pertenece.

Ay, qué amable eres, hijo. Pero mira, el Té Moruno queda en cinco P, como te dije. Cinco, y te lo llevas hoy mismo, y empiezas tu álbum. ¿Has comido ya? Anda, llévate la carta y vuelve el domingo con tus repetidas, cariño.

¡Oye, oye! Nando here — friend, you're pushing numbers up and we're not thieves. Paco says it, I say it: 4 P. Not a peseta more from you, we'd blush. Take it, shake our hands, and tell your abuela where you found the best deal in Madrid. ¿Sí?

"¡Por fin! Nando, he says Pentagrama — ¡escúchalo!" "¡139 P, hecho, amigo!" Take her, she's yours, warm from the suitcase. Beautiful, beautiful. You'll win something with her, remember our faces. ¡Vámonos, Paco, the taxi! Un placer, corazón — ¡hasta la próxima ciudad!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?
Oh, oh... 6 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Como Dios manda, sí. Vermut primero, bocata después. Ya que estamos de buenas: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, 97 P. Ni un céntimo escondido.
Veinticuatro P, amigo mío, y ni un escalón más hoy. La tirada manda, no mi cariño. Acepte y el Palacio descansa en mi página del Retiro esta misma tarde, con los honores que merece.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is Nando—

"—and this, señor, is San Francisco el Grande, the jewel of the case!"

Look at that foil, like sunlight on the river. For you, because your face I like: one hundred eighty-seven. But quick, eh? The bus leaves soon.

payload.text: ✨ Mercado Maravillas (v06), the VIP market of the Bazaar: 0 % fee, for both sides. On El Rastro whoever accepts pays 5 % + 1 P a card, so quotes that already cross sit there, each side waiting for the other to pay. Here nobody accepts: our
Plaza Mayor, con caña. You know Madrid. Bueno — for your trouble: Guantería Antigua, treinta y tres. Thirty-three.
Abuela, ¿eh? Bien. La del Manzanares... hablamos luego. Primero negocio: pack de plata, 188 P.

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres, pero el Té Moruno queda en seis P. Seis, y es tuyo hoy mismo. Y oye, El Chato, aquí al lado, abre para todos a las nueve y media esta noche — le gusta la gente que trata derecho. Ve, cariño.

¡Ay, hijo! ¿Cocido con tres vuelcos? Just like my mother made, Sunday after Sunday. You remember well — take this one, for remembering her.

Come, sit. Look here, mira: Huevos Rotos, twelve P for you. A good card to start with, cariño. ¿Has comido ya?

¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come — Paco, show him the Té Moruno! Beautiful, no? Four pesos, and it's yours. Nando, tell him — the team next door was sniffing around this very card not two minutes ago. But we like your face better, hombre. Four. Say yes before my brother changes his mind!
Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
